what: three independent blind judges; each saw blind/<pattern>.png (real photo + real whiteness w + models A and B, same render) and blind/structures.md, not key.json. Fields A_structure / B_structure / closer_to_real are the judges' raw answers; FS_structure / CAL_structure / closer_set are decoded with key.json.

patterns.notes: A: solid, nearly uniform pale heart with a narrow top notch and a sharp pointed tip that pulls into a short tail, like the real one. It has a brown central seam running from the notch almost to the tip, dark in about the top third and faint below. The real heart has no seam. B: heart outline and notch are there, but the upper middle is a large hollow brown area with nested inner arcs, so it is not a solid white heart. Its bottom is rounded and blunt with no sharp tip, and a brown seam runs down the full axis. A matches the real solid heart with its tip much better.

Both show three nested tiers of arms (outer crescents, middle arms, inner two-lobed heart) split by brown seams. A: the arms are thin bands with wide brown gaps, and the inner lobes curl and are hollow. It reads more like an outline or a tulip fan, and it sits low in the cup. B: the arms are broad, bright white blocks separated by thin, clean brown seams that meet at a sharp bottom tip. This is closer to the real broad white blocks with seams of 2 to 4 mm. Neither has the separate small heart at the pour-start side or the roughly 40 degree tilt, as expected from the symmetric guessed actions.

Both are much dimmer than the real heart, which is solid white with 8 to 10 fine arcs. A: two dim lobes, each with about 3 faint concentric arcs and a bright curl beside the notch. The outline does not close at the bottom: the lobes fade out and do not meet. Instead a long bright stem or tail runs out of the bottom. B: closed heart outline with a notch and a pointed tip. Each lobe has about 3 to 4 nested arcs plus a bright curl at the notch, so a cut near the centre plausibly crosses 4 or more bands. Its lower interior is hollow brown rather than solid white. B gives the closed layered-heart shape. A does not.

A: clear stack of three layers, closed outline with a bottom tip. From the inside out: a small bright two-lobed heart at the top, then a darker middle layer of wings, then an outer crescent shell. There are clear brown seams between the layers, the one between the inner and middle layers being wide. The inner heart is much smaller and narrower than the real top heart. B: large dim body with many thin nested petals, about 4 to 5 on each side, and many narrow seams. It looks more like a feathered rosetta or leaf than three distinct stacked hearts, and the bottom tip is faint. Neither shows the ripple on the outer bottom arc or the 17 degree tilt. A's few layers with wide gaps are closer to the real 'heart on heart plus outer arc' structure.

A: a heart-shaped bright tip at the top and about 6 to 7 pairs of fairly bright V-shaped veins meeting on a central line, which acts as the midrib. An outer crescent arc encloses them and closes to a tip at the bottom. The veins are dense and well contrasted, though there are fewer than the real ~12 pairs and the leaf is shorter than 0.7 D. B: a strong bright midrib runs all the way down as a stem, and there are two curls at the top. Its veins, about 5 to 6 per side, are thin, dim and sparse in a mostly brown interior, so the vein amplitude looks weak. The big dim outer wings dominate. A's dense bright V veins with the heart tip look more like the real leaf. B's long midrib is its only advantage.

B: a clear head curl at the upper left and a thin, continuous S-shaped neck going down the left side. A distinct wing frond of about 6 to 7 V-shaped feathers with brown gaps points to the upper right, matching the real layout. It also has a separate U-shaped body ring underneath, which the real swan does not have. A: a small head curl and a neck that broadens quickly into a diffuse muddy mass. The wing feathers are smeared, low-contrast streaks with no clean V spacing, so it is hard to read. Neither has the real heart-shaped head with a notch. B shows head, neck and wing feathers much more clearly.

Real: solid white heart, about 0.45 of the cup surface, centred (centroid y about 0), deep narrow notch, pointed tip with a fine tail. A: solid cream heart about 0.54 D wide (real about 0.68 D), white about 0.29 of the cup, centroid in the right place (y about 0), clear notch and a pointed tip with a short tail. Its defect is a brown seam down the whole axis, from the notch to the tip; it is strongest in the top third and stays as a thin line below that. The real heart has no seam. B: sits too low (centroid y about +0.13 D, bottom near 0.39 D). It is a hollow U: a tan rim around a large brown V/heart cavity with nested arcs. The bottom is rounded, not pointed. Only the notched top reads as a heart.

Neither model has the separate small heart on the pour side or the roughly 40 degree tilt. Both are symmetric, which was expected. A: sits too low (white centroid y about +0.14 D vs real +0.02, top of the white only at -0.10 D, bottom at 0.41 D, close to the rim). The arms are thin white ribbons with wide brown gaps, and white covers only about 0.20 of the cup (real 0.32). The arms separate clearly, but the pattern looks more like an open tulip than fat white blocks. B: centred (centroid y about 0.02, extent -0.22 to 0.32 D vs real -0.37 to 0.33). It has fat white bands (about 0.24 of the cup) cut by thin dark seams, close to the real 2-4 mm, and an inner heart enclosed by outer wrapping arcs. Arms converge into one tip at the bottom. Block thickness and seam width look much more like the real cup.

Both are far too small and too dark. Real white is about 0.5 of the cup, extending about 0.76 D wide and -0.34 to 0.41 D tall, with a solid white lower half. A and B each have only about 0.15 of the cup visibly milky and almost nothing bright. A: two faint, open lobes about 0.56 D wide, each with about 3-4 faint concentric arcs and bright inner curls at the notch. A bright central stem/tail runs down to about 0.38 D. The outer contour does not close at the bottom, so there is no lower half of the heart. B: slightly smaller (about 0.50 D) but has a closed heart outline: a tan rim that converges to a pointed tip at about 0.28 D. Inside are bright inner curls at the notch and 2-3 nested arcs per lobe. The interior is hollow brown, not white. B reads as a heart with the right outline. A reads as two wings plus a stem.

Real: white spans about 0.78 D across and -0.44 to 0.37 D tall (about 0.42 of the cup). It has a bright top heart, a large heart below and a broad, rounded bottom arc with fine ripples, separated by wide brown gaps. Both models nest their layers inside each other instead of stacking them top to bottom. A: compact (about 0.55 D wide, milky area about 0.13). It has a crisp closed shell with a pointed V bottom, a darker middle layer and a bright inner pair at the top, with clear brown seams between the layers. Its three-layer structure is the clearest. B: larger (about 0.63 D wide, milky area about 0.21, closer to real). Its outer layer is a broad rounded arc with faint multiple ripples, like the real bottom arc. Inside are 2-3 nested V layers and an inner bright pair, but the seams are blurry and low-contrast. On size and the rounded outer arc, B is closer. On crisp layer separation, A is better.

Real: tall rosetta. The heart tip nearly touches the top rim (-0.48 D), with about 12 pairs of fat white V leaflets on thin brown lines, a midrib, side lobes at mid-height and a wide base at about 0.37 D. Both models are under-sized (about 0.56-0.64 D wide vs real about 0.74 D, milky area about 0.23 vs 0.45). B extends a bit lower (stem to 0.38 D), which is a small layout advantage. A: a heart-curl tip at the top that protrudes slightly above the flanking shell, as in the real cup. It has about 6 pairs of crisp, light V leaflets fanning off a midrib, inside a crescent shell that closes to a point at about 0.27 D. B: two large wing lobes that rise higher than the tip (the reverse of the real cup), which leaves an open brown top. Its veins are thin faint streaks on a mostly brown interior; the brown/white ratio is inverted compared with the real leaflets. A long bright midrib runs to the bottom edge. A's rosetta, with white-dominant leaflets and the tip on top, matches the real leaf better. The size difference between A and B is small.

Real: notched heart-shaped head at the upper left (about -0.25, -0.3 D) and a thick S-neck down the left side. A large feathered wing fills the right side and the top, reaching about -0.45 D, with chevron feathers and concentric arcs sweeping round the bottom right. There is no separate round body; white covers about 0.40 of the cup. Both models have a tiny curl for a head at about (-0.15, -0.35) instead of a heart, and the wing reaches only about -0.2 D. A: a continuous neck that widens into a broad, diffuse milky mass on the left and bottom. Its smeared diagonal feathers (about 6-7) run to the upper right. The overall mass distribution is closer to real (centroid about -0.04, -0.03 vs real -0.05, -0.04, slightly larger extent), but the feathers are messy. B: crisp head, thin continuous neck and a compact, sharp feather wing (about 8 leaflets) along a 45 degree axis. However, it sits inside a distinct U-shaped round body ring separated from the wing by a brown gap. That is the separate round body the real cup does not have. B's structure is cleaner; A's layout is closer.

A: solid cream heart with a deep top notch and a sharp tip that ends in a short tail, which reads as the real 大白心. Its flaw is a brown seam along the central axis that runs the whole length from notch to tip: dark in the top third, fainter mid-heart, darker again near the tip. The real heart has no seam. B: the outline has a notch with two curled horns, but the inside is a large hollow brown V reaching down to the bottom and the bottom is round with no tip. It reads as a hollow cup or ring, not a solid heart, and fails the 'has a tip' requirement. B is also smaller and duller.

Both are symmetric (as expected from the guessed actions) and neither has the separate small heart on the pour-start side. A: about 3 arms per side (thin outer crescent, middle arm, central lobes that curl inward) with wide, very clear brown seams. The arms are well separated but thin and spindly, so A looks like a fanned tulip and has none of the real cup's large white masses. B: a clear central heart with a notch, wrapped by a thick bright outer arc plus one inner arm per side. The seams are thinner but clean, and everything meets at the bottom tip. The 'inner heart wrapped by an outer arc' layout and the white mass are closer to the real cup. A wins only on seam width.

Neither has what defines the real cup: about 8-10 fine parallel brown arcs filling each lobe, and a solid white lower half. Both are dim and low-contrast. A: two separate diffuse lobes that never close at the bottom (brown below the center) and run into a long thin stem. Each lobe has about 3-4 faint concentric arcs near the axis. It looks like two wings on a stalk, not a heart. B: a closed heart outline with a notch and tip, and about 3-4 bright inner curls or arcs per lobe. The center and lower half are hollow brown instead of solid white. B at least reads as a heart with some inner layering.

The real cup has a top heart, then a big bright heart, then a wavy bottom arc, with wide brown gaps between layers. A: a bright top piece (two teardrops rather than one heart), a wide dark V gap, a dim middle layer, a narrow seam, then a closed outer arc with a tip. About three stacked layers are recognizable, but the middle 'big heart' is dim and thin, not a bright solid heart. B: the center is 5-6 thin finger streaks fanning from the axis inside a diffuse outer wrap that is open at the top. It reads as a feather or rosetta fan, not stacked hearts, and has no wide inter-layer gaps. Both are much dimmer than the real cup.

A: a clear rosetta with a two-curl heart tip on top, about 6-7 V-shaped leaflets per side separated by distinct brown lines, a central midrib, and a closed outer arc with a tip at the bottom. A barista would call it a leaf, though it has about half the real cup's ~12 leaflet pairs, is dimmer, and is shorter than ~0.7 D. B: a long continuous midrib from top to bottom (good), but only about 4-5 faint, low-contrast leaflets per side. Two big diffuse side wings are open at the top. The vein structure is weak and the overall shape reads more like wings around a stem.

Neither has a heart-shaped head; both heads are small curls at the top-left. A: thin continuous neck down the left, but the body is a muddy, smeared mass. Feather streaks toward the upper right are blurry and broken by a dark hole, so wing and body are not clearly separated. B: a clean S-curved neck from the head down the left, and a crisp wing plume to the upper right with about 6-7 distinct V-shaped feathers and clean brown lines between them. That matches the real wing much better. B's flaw is a distinct round U-shaped body ring under the wing, which the real cup does not have. It is still the more recognizable swan.
